work/assets/strings/en.json and es.json are separate tables, one per language; the README section 'Adding a language' says to copy en.json to <code>.json and translate it.
Fresh sB: Enter on New season gives texts [New season, Slot 1: Empty, Slot 2: Empty, Slot 3: Empty]; Escape gives the title.

Easy + 3 days: coins 60, 'Day 1 of 3', forecast of 3 entries. After the settings were changed to Hard/7, Continue still had season_difficulty easy and season_length 3. A new Hard season had 40 coins.

Forecast has 7 (or 3) entries from sun/cloud/rain/heat; weather and 'Weather:' follow forecast[day-1] (day 2 cloud, seed 9 day 2 heat). Seed 1 gave the same forecast twice; seed 2 gave a different one.

Every Morning I saw (seeds 1, 2, 3, 9, 16, several days) had wholesale prices within base-1..base+2, e.g. seed 1: apples 1, bread 4, cheese 6, fish 7, flowers 5, honey 5. The rows read like 'Apples: 1 a unit, stock 0'.
Apples at 1: coins 50 to 44 to 38, stock [{units 6, days_left 5}] then one batch of 12, and the row reads 'stock 12'. Bread at 4: coins down 24, days_left 1. Honey batch days_left null.

Cheese at 6 with 14 coins: coins and stock unchanged, 'Not enough coins' stays through repeated Enter and is gone after the next Down. Honey 16 lots reach 96 units; a 17th lot changed neither coins (76) nor stock.

Day 1 order null. Day-2+ orders were all units 4/6/8 with pay = units*ref*3/2 (8 bread 72, 6 cheese 99, 6 honey 81, 4 flowers 42, 8 fish 168). Text 'Order: 8 Bread for 72'; accept makes taken true and 'Order taken: ...'; a second accept changed nothing.
After a run that started a Normal season in slot 1, a later run on the same place showed the title [Day Market, New season, Continue, Records, ...] and the slot row 'Slot 1: Day 1 of 7, 50 coins'.

Season saved at the day 2 Morning (seed 1), then Continue in a later run with --seed 77: day, coins, reputation, stock, stall, prices, upgrades, forecast, wholesale, order and texts all identical. Enter on empty slot 2 changed nothing.

Escape on Morning, Stall and Day gives Paused [Paused, Resume, Title]. In the Day the clock stood at 2 for 99 paused ticks. Resume and Escape go back to the same state. Title gives the title with the slot at 50 coins, not the 44 left after a lot bought that Morning.
Stall opens with cursor (0,0), selected apples, and texts Stall, Good: Apples, Price: 4, Stock: 6 (the apples in stock), Crates: 0 of 8.
From (0,0): Left and Down change nothing; Up gives y 1 and a second Up stays; Right x6 stops at x 5.
next_good x6: bread, cheese, fish, flowers, honey, apples; prev_good: honey, flowers. The Good/Price/Stock texts followed each step (e.g. Good: Cheese, Price: 11, Stock: 0).
put at (5,1) adds {x 5, y 1, flowers} and Crates: 1 of 8; put on the occupied cell and take on the empty cell change nothing; take removes the crate. After 8 crates a 9th put changed nothing.
Apples: price_up x10 stops at 12; price_down x15 stops at 1; the Price text follows each change.
Day 1 stall and prices (apples 5, 3 crates) were the same on the day 2 Stall, and the same after a save and Continue in a later run (diff empty).
Enter on Stall: screen day, clock 0, speed slow, texts 08:00 and Speed: Slow, taken/served/walked_out/passed 0, visitors holds the 79-entry list.
12 visitor lists (872 visitors): ids 1..n in order, minutes strictly rising within 0..479, types among the four, distinct wants 2/1/2/3. Seed 1 gave the same list twice; seed 2 gave another.

In one run: slow +1 minute at 20 ticks, fast every 5, rush every tick, hold none (tick goes on, screen day). Leftover progress carried over: slow 30 ticks then fast reached clock 2 after 3 fast ticks. Time and Speed texts followed.
finish given at day tick 300: by the next tick screen evening, clock 480, with taken, served, walked_out, passed, sales, coins and reputation equal to the rush run's.
The same day at slow (9600 ticks), fast, rush, a mix (slow, fast, hold, rush, slow, fast) and fast+finish: identical coins, taken, served, walked_out, passed, sales, stock and evening texts.
My own simulation of the brief's minute rules, fed the game's visitor list, matched the game's aisle (x = clock - m, off at m+6), queue and tills at every minute of 14 days (0 mismatches).
Covered by the minute-by-minute match. On a day with Sign removed from the reference, it fails to match, so back-row looking is really being tested.
Apples crate at column 2. At price 4: cooks arriving at 20 and 23 held 2 apples at 4 at clock 22 and 25, budget_left 32. At 5 no cook took any. Tourists took 1 at 5 and at 6, none at 7.
The minute-by-minute match (which checks budget and available units) held on 14 days, including a 96-honey day with two tills and a day with queues of 4.
The match covers passed counts and queue joins; queue entries' joined = arrival + 6 at every compared minute.

The match covers till ends (s+2+goods), coins, taken, served, reputation, sales and bargain discount. With apples batches days_left 4 (10 units) and 5 (6 units), 6 sold came from the days_left-4 batch.
Covered by the minute-by-minute match (till ending at m takes the queue front in m; a visitor leaving the aisle at m goes straight to a free till).
Seed 3 day 6: walked_out 5 with queues up to 4. The reference (reputation -2 each, goods freed) matched every minute. No queued visitor's wait ever reached its patience.
At 480 the screen is evening; visitors left on the aisle or queue were not counted in walked_out or passed (the reference, which drops them, matched the evening counts).
With Second till: tills has 2 entries; 14 minutes had both tills serving at once. The reference with two tills (till 1 first) matched every minute; with one till it did not.

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
